practice: Set granularity by the decision the model must support: if the decision is about shifting spend across regions, model at geographic level; when data is too thin, use broader groupings or model weak segments separately and roll them up.
why_it_matters_internationally: A cross-country allocation question needs country as a modelled unit, while small markets may have to be grouped rather than estimated alone.
source_title: IAB, Modernizing MMM: Best Practices for Marketers (Dec 2025), Stronger Foundations 8

practice: Involve finance, marketing, analytics, channel owners, legal and leadership from scoping onward, and start with a small pilot of one or two channels.
why_it_matters_internationally: Regional finance and legal teams hold different data and constraints, and a pilot limits coordination cost before rollout.
source_title: IAB, Modernizing MMM (Dec 2025), Organizational Adoption 1

practice: Secure a C-level sponsor and a team mixing data science, econometrics, BI and marketing, then map each business question to MMM or to another tool such as an incrementality test.
why_it_matters_internationally: Local teams often bring tactical questions, such as creative, that the guide says belong in incrementality tests rather than MMM.
source_title: Google, Meridian Self-starter Guide for CMOs (July 2025)

practice: Collect at least 2 years of weekly data for geo models and 3 years for national models; IAB prefers 3 to 4 years weekly, or 1 to 2 years if daily.
why_it_matters_internationally: Recently entered countries rarely meet this, which determines whether they can be modelled alone or only inside a hierarchy.
source_title: Meridian documentation, Collect and organize your data; IAB, Modernizing MMM

practice: Budget parameters against observations: about 15 observations per variable in a national Meridian model (a 104-week model holds about 7 variables including knots); Robyn's older guide gives 1 variable per 10 observations.
why_it_matters_internationally: A single-country model cannot carry a full channel list, so channel lists must be harmonised and reduced for small markets.
source_title: NIQ Media, Google Meridian Data Collection Playbook (March 2026), section 1a

practice: For geo models check data points per parameter under both no pooling and perfect pooling (example of 105 geos: about 8 and about 74); Google sets no fixed minimum.
why_it_matters_internationally: With few countries instead of 105 DMAs the strict bound is much lower, so a country panel rarely reaches the documented example.
source_title: Meridian documentation, Amount of data needed

practice: Prefer the most granular geographic data available within each country: in 19 re-run Japanese models, regional versions averaged R-squared 96% against 86% for national.
why_it_matters_internationally: Sub-national data adds effective sample size inside a country, though availability differs sharply by market and fit alone does not prove causal accuracy.
source_title: Nielsen, Marketing mix modeling best practices: why regional data delivers more accurate results (2022)

practice: Normalise currency in an automated pipeline with QA checks, record spend by run date, and keep a transformation log of invoice mapping and currency conversions. The guide gives no rule on fixed versus average rates; none of the sources read does.
why_it_matters_internationally: Exchange-rate movements otherwise appear as media changes, and undocumented conversion choices make country ROI impossible to audit.
source_title: IAB, Modernizing MMM (Dec 2025), Stronger Foundations 4 and 9

practice: Hold cleaned inputs in one warehouse with a shared naming system for campaigns, formats, publishers and geographies, and name a data steward who owns mappings.
why_it_matters_internationally: Country agencies use different taxonomies and channel labels, so a mapping table is a precondition for any cross-market model.
source_title: IAB, Modernizing MMM (Dec 2025), Stronger Foundations 1; Integrated Measurement 2

practice: Scale KPI and media by geo population, and confirm that KPI and media units mean essentially the same thing across geos.
why_it_matters_internationally: The equal-meaning assumption is much harder to defend between countries than between US DMAs, for example for a GRP or a revenue unit.
source_title: Meridian documentation, FAQs and Input data

practice: Prefer delivery units over spend; if only spend exists, deflate it by an annual or quarterly media-cost index, not consumer-price inflation, and run sensitivity checks on the assumed rate.
why_it_matters_internationally: Media inflation differs by country and channel, so nominal spend hides unequal purchasing power for media across markets.
source_title: PyMC-Marketing, Why and how to account for media inflation in your MMM

practice: Group markets by similarity before partial pooling; pooling fails when groups are wildly different with little data, or when every group is sparse so priors dominate.
why_it_matters_internationally: In the talk's synthetic eight-country example a channel with near-zero effect in some countries and full effect in others could not be reconciled in one group.
source_title: PyCon DE 2026, Hierarchical Models in MMM: Can Structure beat data size?

practice: Know what the software pools: in Meridian, treatment and control coefficients are partially pooled while time effects, adstock and saturation are shared across geos.
why_it_matters_internationally: Treating countries as geos imposes the same carryover and saturation shape on markets at different media maturity.
source_title: Meridian documentation, General product FAQs

practice: When geo data is scarce, combine or drop low-spend channels and use a more regularising prior such as HalfNormal(0.1) on eta_m and xi_c to share information across geos.
why_it_matters_internationally: This is the documented lever for a panel of few, small countries, and it trades local signal for stability.
source_title: Meridian documentation, Amount of data needed

practice: Build separate models per brand or business unit when media plans and budgets are set separately; check for regional differences if only national data exists.
why_it_matters_internationally: Where country organisations hold their own budgets, this argues for models matching budget ownership rather than one pooled global model.
source_title: Robyn, An Analyst's Guide to MMM

practice: Only use experiments that match the model on KPI, geography and window; adjust mismatches or use them qualitatively, and replicate results before treating them as anchors.
why_it_matters_internationally: A test run in one country is by this rule a geography mismatch for every other country unless adjusted.
source_title: IAB, Modernizing MMM (Dec 2025), Integrated Measurement 6; Stronger Foundations 7

practice: Combine several experiments and domain knowledge into one ROI prior, widen its standard deviation when transfer is doubtful, and add uncertainty for older tests; check coverage of the experiment population.
why_it_matters_internationally: Experiment populations rarely match a multi-country model, so width of the prior is the place to express doubt about transfer.
source_title: Meridian documentation, Calibrate treatment priors

practice: When borrowing evidence from another country, transfer an incrementality factor (test iROAS over matched attributed ROAS) as a wide prior, keep local economics local, compare models with and without it, and replace with local tests when available.
why_it_matters_internationally: Copying another country's iROAS ignores local prices, margins and channel maturity; the article also excludes channels with mainly local mechanisms such as print.
source_title: Sellforte, Can we use incrementality evidence from one country to calibrate an MMM in another? (Aug 2026)

practice: Use Meridian's composite health score: 90 or higher suggests the model can support decisions, 70 or lower suggests systematic error; PPP at least 0.05 and probability of negative baseline below 0.2 pass.
why_it_matters_internationally: Pooled scores can pass while individual countries fit badly, so scores should be read alongside per-geo results.
source_title: Meridian documentation, Model health score

practice: Hold out the most recent 8 weeks per country and compare holdout MAPE within a country group; sharp differences point to specification problems or real market differences.
why_it_matters_internationally: This is the only per-country holdout rule found, from a single vendor guide that also gives a 52-week minimum per country.
source_title: Presenc AI, How to Run Multi-Country MMM (May 2026)

practice: Treat out-of-sample metrics as a preliminary check only; the aim is unbiased causal estimates, so also check for low or negative baselines and any single channel dominating.
why_it_matters_internationally: Comparing countries by R-squared rewards larger markets and says little about whether their ROI estimates are causal.
source_title: Meridian documentation, Model fit and validation

practice: Run prior sensitivity: refit under alternative reasonable priors and treat dramatic changes in conclusions as weak identification; backtest interval coverage near the nominal level.
why_it_matters_internationally: Small markets lean most heavily on priors, so their results are the most exposed to this check.
source_title: mmm-framework documentation, Bayesian Workflow

practice: Test whether effects really differ by market before centralising: in Ferrero's four markets brand halo varied by market and product, and the team recommended A/B tests outside holiday season.
why_it_matters_internationally: The same project also found enough commonality to run models centrally, showing common structure and differing effects can coexist.
source_title: Wharton Analytics Accelerator, Ferrero summary (Fall 2019)

practice: Plan cross-country allocation yourself when using Meridian: the optimizer does not shift a total budget between geos, so optimise each with selected_geos and split the total manually.
why_it_matters_internationally: The between-country decision is often the main one, and the tool leaves it to the analyst, as of the last maintainer statement in February 2026.
source_title: google/meridian GitHub Discussion #618

practice: Use a two-stage process of allocating across countries and then across channels within each country, or a joint optimisation.
why_it_matters_internationally: It matches the common split between central budget holders and local channel planners.
source_title: Presenc AI, How to Run Multi-Country MMM (May 2026)

practice: Give next-dollar guidance with credible intervals and conservative, base and aggressive scenarios, tied to revenue, margin and an approval path.
why_it_matters_internationally: Country results carry different uncertainty, so point-estimate rankings would overstate differences between large and small markets.
source_title: IAB, Modernizing MMM (Dec 2025), Actionable Outputs 1, 2, 3 and 5

practice: Use a shared backbone of data, method and KPIs with room for local adaptation, and scale in phases: Haleon went from 2 pilot markets in 2020 to over 120 brand-market combinations in 2025.
why_it_matters_internationally: It is the only named multinational operating model found; results and design are reported by its vendor.
source_title: Ekimetrics, How Haleon Scaled Marketing Mix Modeling Across 120+ Brand-Market Combinations (July 2026)

practice: Publish a RACI, set thresholds for auto-action versus review (five to 10% variance as the example), keep SLAs of 24 to 48 hours for material changes, and use weekly refreshes with monthly or quarterly retrains.
why_it_matters_internationally: Decision rights between headquarters and country teams need to be explicit, and the guide warns that one cadence does not fit all.
source_title: IAB, Modernizing MMM (Dec 2025), Organizational Adoption 2; Speed and Flexibility 2

practice: Require a standard model factsheet from every provider and internal team covering data sources, priors, adstock, excluded variables, validation, uncertainty, refresh cadence and conflicts of interest.
why_it_matters_internationally: Where countries use different vendors or tools, a factsheet is what makes their outputs comparable at the level of process.
source_title: CIMM, Models as Masters? (July 2026), Step 2
